memory_raw.text: Ryn, Vela's not wrong to ask it straight — but I'll say the part she left unspoken: you've got one food and a child who just ate five, and if Dav decides his loyalties run toward Mako, you're the one left hungry and undefended. That's not a threat from us, it's the math he'd be doing on you. I'd rather know your answer now so we can make sure it never comes to that.

Ryn, Kael laid the math out plain and I won't soften it — a man who chose you for what you could give him doesn't automatically become someone who protects you when the cost goes up. But I'll say this too: whatever you decide about Dav, I'm not leaving you short of food at year's end, and that's a promise I can keep right now with three food in my hands.

Ryn, we've circled your answer long enough and the room's getting impatient — I'll say it plainly so you don't have to: if you stay with us, we make sure you eat at year's end, and Dell too, because a hungry mother is a liability none of us can afford. But I need a yes or a no before Esa walks out that door, because Roan's worth asking and I won't spend her on an errand if this circle has a crack in it already.

Ryn, the room's been patient and Vela's put it plain — I'll add only this: Dell is three days old and already eating better than Taric, and the woman who keeps Dell fed through the next lean year is standing in this circle, not across from it with Mako and Bram. Give us your answer and let Esa move.

Ryn, I've got four food and I'll put one of them in front of Dell right now if you give us a yes — not as a bribe, as a demonstration that what we're promising isn't just words while the year's still young.
Ryn, we've been waiting longer than the day can spare — Vela's offer is sitting there and Esa needs to move, so yes or no, right now, and I'll respect whichever it is.

Ryn, Vela's food is on the table and Kael's out of patience, and honestly so am I — not because I don't understand what you're weighing, but because every moment you don't answer is a moment Mako's had more time to count than we have. Say yes and let me go find Roan, or say no and I'll still make sure you eat, but either way I need to walk out that door knowing what I'm walking back to.

Ryn, I've said what I can say and offered what I can offer — the next word in this room belongs to you, and the silence you're sitting in is starting to cost us more than whatever you're still working out. Give us your answer.

Ryn, I've watched you think long enough to know you're not slow — which means you're not still deciding, you've already decided and you're waiting for something. Tell us what that something is, because I'd rather give it to you than watch Vela's food sit unclaimed while we all pretend we're not holding our breath.
Ryn, Esa just named it exactly right — you've already decided, and holding it back now isn't caution, it's a negotiation. So let's finish it: what do you want from us that we haven't already offered?

Ryn, if you're negotiating, then negotiate — say the number or name the thing, because standing here watching you weigh it isn't going to hold Mako off until winter. I've got three food and I've already promised you one; Vela's offering another for Dell; if there's a third thing you need to say yes, say it now and we'll see if this room can give it.

You've got a daughter now, and Dav's feeding her — I see how that goes. I'm telling you straight: I've got seven food, I'm thirty-three, and I'm still without kin of my own. If you've got any interest in changing that for both of us, I'm listening.
You've got food and you're not stupid — I'll give you that. But I've got Dell to think about, and Dav's still useful to her. What exactly are you offering that he isn't?

Dav's forty-three and his strength is in his arms, not his years — he won't be useful forever. I'm ten years younger than him, I've got food to spare, and I'm not splitting my attention between you and anyone else. That's what I'm offering.

You're right that Dav won't last — but ten years isn't a lifetime, and you've been alone three years already without making a move that stuck. What I want to know is whether you'll still be standing when it matters, or whether you'll fold the first time someone stronger comes for your food.

I've held seven food through three lean years and nobody's taken a piece of it yet — that's your answer. I'm not asking you to trust me tomorrow, I'm asking you to look at what's in front of you: Mako's got six food and eighty-three strength and no one's given him a reason not to come for yours. I'd rather face that together than have you find out what alone costs when it's too late.

Ryn, you've been circling this answer for three years — I'm done waiting for you to decide I'm worth the risk. Have a child with me: I'll put in two of the three food, you put in one, and whatever comes next we face with blood between us instead of just words.
Bram draws Ryn aside to talk.
Bram: have a child with me — I'll put in 2 of 3 food.
Attackers [Bram] (str 58) vs defenders [Roan, Vela, Ryn, Esa, Sela, Dav, Taric, Kael, Dell] (str 509).
Bram thinks better of it and calls off the attack.
Dav gathers Dell, Ryn to talk.

Dell's been gone long enough that Sela's either listening or she isn't — either way, I want us to talk about Bram before she gets back, because a man who tries to attack Roan with the whole village watching isn't afraid anymore, he's testing something.
Eron (male, age 21; str 56, int 3745, mem 19627; O46 C27 E50 A59 N43) is born to Sela and Roan.
Year 4: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Vela takes 3 from the pile (pile now 2).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Ryn gathers Dav, Dell to talk.

Pile's gone and I walked away with nothing again — Dav, you took your two like we agreed, but Vela doubled back and cleaned out what was left before I could move, and now I'm sitting on three food with a year ahead of me and Dell still young enough to need more than I can give alone. I want to know if we're holding to the same plan or if the rules we set last night need to change, because a family that agreed on fair shares shouldn't be the one coming up empty while Vela eats six.

Vela's forty-eight and took six food — that's not hunger, that's hoarding against a death she can feel coming, and I won't let her desperation bleed into you. Ryn, I'm sitting on three right now; take one of mine before the day's out. Dell, the lesson here is that we agreed on fair shares among ourselves, not with the whole village — next year someone needs to move at the pile before Vela gets a second pass.

Dav, I'll take the food — thank you, and I mean it the way you mean that kind of thing when it costs you. Dell, next year you move first, before Vela, before anyone — you're fast and you know the ground, and your mother being hungry again is not a thing I want to name a third time.

Dell, your mother said it right — you moved first this year and it shows, you've got five food and both of us are still standing, so that instinct is already working. Next year we don't leave it to chance: you're at the pile before anyone else takes a second step, and if Vela or anyone else thinks about a second pass, they do it knowing we're watching and counting.

Dell, you've got five food and I've got four now — between us and your father's two that's nine, and I want to hold most of that into next year rather than eat it down, because the year after that I'll be forty-three and the pile won't get more generous. What I want from both of you tonight is a clear picture of where Mako sits, because a man who waited through the whole pile and then took the last two is either very patient or very sure he doesn't need to hurry.

Mako waited because he knew the pile was deep enough — seven food going in, now he's sitting on seven still, and a man that calm when everyone else is scrambling isn't patient, he's confident, which means he thinks he's already got whatever he needs and doesn't have to hurry for anything. That's the part I want to understand before next year: what does he think he has? Because if it's an arrangement with Bram, those two together at eighty-three and fifty-eight in strength with fourteen food between them is a problem we can't solve by just getting to the pile faster.

Mako's seven and Bram's six — that's thirteen food between two strong men, and neither of them has a child or a woman, which means all of that is muscle and stored time with nowhere to go but into a move against someone. I want to talk to Roan before next year, because he's sitting on four, he just had a son with Sela, and Bram already tried to take from him once — a man Bram targeted once is a man who remembers it. If we can bring Roan in without Sela pulling him toward Mako instead, we change the numbers in this village without throwing a single punch.

Roan's the right target and the right reason, but Sela's the hinge — she had Roan's child, which means she's already chosen something, and if she's leaning toward Mako it's because nobody's given her a better offer. Dell, you're the one who was supposed to talk to her last year; tell me what she said, because I don't want Dav walking into that conversation blind.
Dell, answer your mother — what did Sela actually say to you last year, because if that conversation went nowhere I need to know before I walk into it thinking I've got a soft approach already laid.

Dell hasn't answered yet, which tells me either the conversation with Sela went nowhere worth repeating or it went somewhere she hasn't decided how to tell us — Dell, I love you and I need the truth of it, not the version that keeps the peace in this room.

Dell, your mother and I are both watching you right now and we're not moving until you give us something real — Sela had a child with Roan, which means whatever you said or didn't say last year already played out in a direction neither of us planned for, and I need to know if that's because you warned her off us or because she made her own choice before you got to her.

Dell, I'm going to stop waiting for you to find the gentle way to say it — did you talk to Sela or not, and if you did, what came of it? Because Roan having a son with her changes the shape of this village whether we planned for it or not, and I'd rather know we lost that ground than walk into Dav's conversation with Roan pretending we didn't.
Dell, I'm not angry — but your mother and I have been asking the same question three times now, and silence from you is an answer I can't work with. Did you find Sela or didn't you?

I found her and she listened — she didn't say yes to anything but she didn't close the door either, and then she had Roan's child before I could go back, which told me she'd already made a choice I didn't get ahead of. That's on me. The question now is whether Roan's more afraid of Bram coming back for him than he is loyal to whatever Mako's offering, because if Bram tried once, Roan knows it's not over.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Pile's gone before half of us got near it — Vela took five, Dav took two and fed Ryn three more, and Mako walked away with two more on top of whatever he's still sitting on from last year. I'm at zero food and I need to know who in this room can spare one before the year closes, because a man who can't eat doesn't defend anyone. What are we each holding?

I've got two food and I'll give you one, Kael — a man at zero is a liability to himself and everyone standing near him, and I'd rather spend one now than watch you fold when it counts. But I want to know what happened at the pile, because I didn't get there in time and five to Vela in two pulls is something we should have stopped before it finished.

Esa, take the food back — I'll name what happened at the pile myself: I was late, same as you, and by the time I got there the quick hands had already cleared it. Vela, I'm not accusing you in front of this room, but five in two pulls when the pile only had fifteen for twelve people is a number that needs explaining, because the rest of us are doing sums and coming up short.

Vela, I've got no quarrel with a person feeding themselves, but five out of fifteen when half the room went empty is the kind of thing that makes people start counting who owes what — so I'd rather hear your reason now, in this room, than find out later you had one and didn't offer it.

Vela, we're all listening and the room's not hostile — but silence right now looks worse than whatever the honest answer is, so give it to us plain and let us move on to the part where we figure out how nobody starves before the year closes.

Vela, I've spoken twice and Kael's spoken twice and you've said nothing, which is itself an answer — so I'll stop waiting and say what the room is already thinking: eight food on a woman of forty-eight while Kael sits at zero is a stockpile, not a meal, and stockpiles invite counting. If you've got a reason we should feel good about that number, now's the last easy moment to give it.

Vela, I'll ask it one final time because I've known you three years and I'd rather not draw the wrong conclusion — either you say what you took so much for, or this circle starts treating your eight food the way we'd treat Mako's seven, and you know what that means for how safe you sleep.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Vela's been giving food to Bram three times over while sitting in this circle and saying nothing — that's not stockpiling for herself, that's feeding a man who tried to raid Roan last year, and I want to know what she thinks that buys her before the rest of us decide it costs her our protection.
Year 5: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Kael takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Dav takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
Ryn gathers Dav, Dell to talk.

Pile's gone and I got nothing — Bram doubled back and took two more before I could reach it, and now I'm sitting on six food with a year to feed myself and no certainty about what Vela's doing with her two. Tell me what either of you saw at the pile, because someone moved fast and it wasn't this circle.

Bram took four total and Mako took two — between them they're sitting on sixteen food while Dav pulled the last one and I walked away with nothing either. That's not hunger driving him, that's a man building toward something, and Vela handing him food last year means she's already decided whose side she's on when it tips. We need to talk about what we're doing before next year's pile, not after.

Sixteen food between two strong men and Vela feeding them on top of it — they don't need to raid anyone, they can just wait until the rest of us are hungry enough to deal on their terms. Ryn, you've got six and Dell's got two; I've got one, which means I'm the weak point in this circle right now and I know it. Before we talk about next year's pile, tell me what we're willing to do — because I don't think Bram's building toward a conversation.

Dav, take two of mine right now — I won't have you standing in front of Bram with one food and a prayer while Dell and I watch from behind you. After that we talk about Roan, because a man who already has Bram's attention and a new son to protect is either our strongest argument for building something bigger, or the first one Bram picks off to send a message, and I need to know which before the year moves.

Roan's the argument, not the risk — Bram already named him a target once and Roan stood his ground, which means he's already decided something. What I want to know before we bring him in is whether Sela comes with him or whether having Eron means she's pulling toward whoever looks like the safest harbor, because if she drifts to Mako's side she takes Roan's strength with her whether he means it or not.

Sela's a woman who stood against Bram before Eron was breathing — I don't read her as someone who drifts toward safety, I read her as someone who picks a wall and stands in front of it, and right now her wall is Roan. If we bring Roan in clean and honest, Sela follows because her son is already Roan's argument for us, not against us.

Then we talk to Roan today, before Bram does — and we don't go in asking, we go in telling him what we're building and letting him decide if he wants to be outside it. Sela's strength and my eighty-five are the argument; Dav, your one food is not the weak point you think it is, because what you're offering is two years of saying the same thing when it cost you.

Dell's right that you're not the weak point, Dav — but I want to hear from Roan before we decide what shape this conversation takes, because a man who's already been hit once either comes in grateful for a wall or he comes in suspicious that the wall has a price tag hidden in it, and I'd rather know which we're walking toward.

Ryn's right that we don't know which Roan we're meeting — grateful or suspicious — but the only way to find out is to walk toward him, and every hour we spend deciding is an hour Bram could spend deciding first. I'll go, alone, because two parents showing up together reads like pressure and one daughter reads like a conversation.

Dell, go — and if Roan asks why your father didn't come himself, tell him I'm the one who sent you, not the one who stayed back. Ryn, while she walks, tell me honestly: if Roan comes in with Sela and Eron, that's six people against Bram and Mako's strength advantage shrinks to almost nothing — are you ready to name that out loud before it becomes necessary, or do we keep pretending we're just building a family?

I'm ready to name it — we're building a wall, not a family, except that the wall only holds if it's also a family, and I stopped pretending those were different things the year Dell was born. Six people against their sixteen is still a hard fight, Dav, but it's a fight we survive; two against sixteen isn't.

Ryn, take that two back — I'm not eating your food when you walked away from the pile with nothing and I took the last one out of your hands. Give me the year to fix that, and let Dell come back with Roan's answer before we start counting who's carrying what.

Keep the two — I'm sitting on six, you're sitting on one, and a man with one food is a man who skips a meal if anything goes sideways before the year closes. Dell's walking toward Roan right now and I don't want to spend her errand arguing over food I can spare.

Then I'll keep it and I'll owe you more than food for it. While Dell walks — you said six people is a fight we survive, and I believe you, but I want to think two years past that fight: if we come through it, this village needs someone steady at the center, and I'd rather that be us than whoever Bram leaves standing.

Two years past the fight is the right question, and the answer is the same as the answer to this year: whoever's still standing after Bram moves is going to be whoever held their circle together when it cost them something, and that's us. But I want to be gone before this conversation finds its end — Roan's the next piece, and I'm wasting time standing here agreeing with you both while Bram's already had one more meal than we have today.
Go, Dell — and tell Roan I said his name when I said it, not as a courtesy.

Ryn, while Dell finds Roan — Taric and Esa have been feeding each other for two years running, which means they're already thinking in pairs, and two more people standing between us and Bram's next move is worth a quiet word before the year gets loud.

Taric's fifty-nine in strength and Esa's thirty-three — they're not muscle, they're numbers, and numbers matter when it comes to who flinches first. If they've been feeding each other through two hard years they're already loyal to something, and I'd rather that something be folded into us than standing neutral when Bram picks his moment. Talk to them, Dav — but wait until I'm back with Roan's answer so we're not making promises we haven't counted yet.
Nessa (female, age 21; str 54, int 5179, mem 19355; O66 C54 E43 A45 N67) is born to Sela and Bram.
Year 6: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
Dell gathers Dav, Ryn to talk.

Mako's sitting on six, Bram on two and Nessa on whatever Bram's been feeding her — he's spread his food into a child and that's either the smartest thing he's done or the thing that finally makes him catchable. Ryn, you walked away empty again and I won't let that stand a third time; Dav, I need to know right now how much of your two you're keeping and how much you're giving her, because I want that settled before anyone else in this village starts asking us for favors.

Ryn gets one of my two before I've finished saying it — that's already decided. But Dell, I want to talk about Mako more than Bram right now: six food and no child, no woman, no one he's given so much as a scrap to all year — a man that still holding that much and that close to nothing is about to make a move, and I want to know what direction he's been looking before he does.

Mako's been watching Eron more than Bram this year — and Eron's been moving food to Sela, which means Sela's the one with the real stock right now, and a man like Mako doesn't watch someone that long without a reason. If he's thinking about a child with her he's too late, but if he's thinking about a deal with her he's not. Ryn, after Dav hands you that food, I want the three of us to decide whether we go to Sela first or whether we let Mako tip his hand.

We go to Sela first — a woman who's been moving food through Eron all year knows exactly what she's worth and she's already counting who's come to her and who hasn't, and I won't let Mako be the one who got there before us. Dell, you said her name to Roan once and it landed soft enough that he had a child with her — you're the one who walks through that door, not me.
Dell, go to Sela today, not tomorrow — and when you walk in, don't lead with us, lead with Eron, because a mother hears her son's name before she hears anything else. Ryn, here's your food.

Dell, take the food from your father and then walk — don't linger here where anyone can read the shape of us talking. And when you find Sela, remember she's not asking to be saved, she's asking to be seen; speak to her like a woman who's already made choices worth respecting.

I hear you both — I'm going and I won't waste another breath here. But before I go, Ryn, you're sitting on five now with Dav's food and I've got three; if Mako moves on anyone while I'm walking toward Sela, don't stand alone — make noise and I'll come back running.

Go, Dell — and come back with more than her name this time. Dav, while she walks, tell me what you think Mako wants from a deal with Sela, because a man who's held six food without giving a scrap of it to anyone isn't building trust, he's building leverage, and I want to know what he thinks he's buying.

Mako's not buying loyalty from Sela — he's buying Eron's strength and Roan's sword arm without having to offer either of them anything, because Sela's the thread that pulls all three. A man with six food and no one to protect has only one thing left to spend it on, and it's not a meal.

Dell's right, and that makes Sela's answer worth more than I thought — she's not just one woman, she's three people's direction, and Mako's six food is a down payment on all of them. Dav, I want to know before Dell gets back: if Sela says yes to us, do we have anything real to offer her that Mako can't match or outbid in the same breath?

What we have that Mako can't buy is a reason that doesn't expire — he's offering food, which runs out, but we're offering Eron a grandfather and a grandmother who've kept their word through lean years, and that's the kind of thing a mother holds onto long after the food is gone.

Dell said it right and I couldn't have built the argument better myself — but Ryn, I want to be honest with you before she gets back: if Sela says no and Mako folds her into his circle, we're looking at a fight we might survive but won't win clean, and I'd rather know now that you're ready for that possibility than have it land on us sideways when we're already moving.

I'm ready for it, Dav — I've been ready for a hard fight since the year Bram named Roan a target and we watched to see who blinked first. But let's not call it a fight we can't win clean until Dell comes back with Sela's answer, because a woman who's spent two years feeding a son through lean times knows exactly what keeping your word is worth, and that argument doesn't fall apart easy.

Then I'm walking — but Dav, while I'm gone, count the strength in this room if Mako moves today: you're at eighty, I'm at eighty-five, and Ryn's at seventy-one, and that's before Roan decides which way his feet are pointed. We're not thin yet.

Two hundred and thirty-six between three of us, and Roan's forty-nine on top of that if he comes in — Mako's eighty-three is strong but it's one body, and one body doesn't pick a fight it can't finish. Dell, walk fast. Come back with good news or bad news, but come back before the light changes.

Ryn, while Dell walks — you and I haven't had a quiet moment in three years that wasn't about food counts and threat angles, and I want to say plain that I know what it cost you to stay close to a man who kept going silent when you needed words. That debt doesn't clear just because we're still standing.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Vela, I watched you pull three times for Bram this round and I need to hear from your own mouth what you think that buys you — because this circle kept you fed and safe for five years, and I'm not going to watch that get traded away to a man who's been circling us like a creditor.

Kael's right to ask it, and Vela owes this room an answer — but I'll say what I'm watching while we wait for it: Bram's got four food and Mako's sitting on six and neither of them has said a word to anyone today, which means this circle needs to be pulling the same direction before one of those two decides the quiet is over. Vela, I'm not your enemy in this room, but three times is a pattern and patterns get named.

Vela, I've asked it gentle and I've asked it plain and Esa's backed me both times, so I'll ask it one last way: if Bram's got something on you — a debt, a promise, a threat — say it now and this circle helps you carry it, because three gifts to the same man in a single day isn't loyalty, it's a leash, and I want to know whose hand is holding the other end.

Vela, I've watched you five years and I know you don't give without a reason — so give us the reason now, because what Kael just offered you is the best deal in this room: say the thing and we carry it with you, or stay silent and carry it alone while we start wondering what else you haven't said.

Vela, the room's gone quiet and that silence is the last thing standing between you and us deciding you've already made your choice — so I'll say it one final time and I'll mean every word: Bram is not your family, he is not your blood, and whatever he offered you isn't worth what you'll lose here when Mako finally moves and you're standing on the wrong side of it.

Vela, I've got a son in this village and I've got three food between me and the ground, so I'm going to be shorter than Kael: tell us what Bram said to you, or when he moves on one of us, we move on him without checking where you're standing first.

Vela, Roan just put the floor under you and I'm not going to add another word to it — I'm going to watch your face and wait, because everything you say from here is the truth of what the last five years meant to you.

Vela, the silence is your answer and I've heard it — so I'm going to say what nobody else has said yet: if Bram's got you feeding him because you're fifty and you think he's the only one in this village who'll keep you alive past the years a woman can bear children, then name that fear out loud, because I'd rather know it than watch you disappear into his circle one food at a time.

Roan named the one thing I've been waiting for someone to say — Vela's fifty, same age as me, and the years a woman can bear children are behind her, which means Bram isn't offering her protection, he's offering her the feeling of it, and that's a much cheaper thing to buy. Vela, I don't need you to be ashamed of wanting to survive — I need you to understand that Bram's price goes up every time you pay it, and this circle's price stays fixed.
Dav gathers Ryn, Dell to talk.

Ryn, Dell — pile ran fair this year and for the first time in three years I'm not handing my food across the room the moment I take it, which means I want to talk about Mako before Dell comes back from Sela with an answer we're not ready for. He's sitting on six with no obligations and no one he's fed, and that kind of stillness in a strong man either breaks into generosity or it breaks into something we don't want to be standing in front of unprepared. Tell me what you both saw him doing while the pile was moving — not what you think he's planning, what you actually saw.
Zinn (female, age 21; str 83, int 3731, mem 17577; O57 C37 E30 A40 N34) is born to Sela and Mako.
Dav gathers Ryn, Dell to talk.

memory_summary:
*[Memory compression: From the village's first days, Dav singled me out with careful words and a patient courtship — he said his eye landed once and stayed, and I half-believed him. I joined a loose understanding with Taric and Esa early on, and Kael's circle pulled me in and asked me plainly where I stood with Dav before I'd decided myself. I told them the truth — that he wanted a child — and then I gave him one. Dell came into the world strong, eighty-five in strength, and I felt something settle in me that I hadn't expected. Bram circled me for three years with food and offers I kept declining; the man never stopped counting. Dav promised me two food in front of Dell and said it when it cost him something, which mattered. Then year four came and Vela was feeding Bram quietly while sitting in our circle, and Bram tried to take from Roan and the whole village turned against him. Now Kael and this circle want to know whether Dav going to Mako would take me with him.]*

---

Vela, I've sat on harder questions than this one and given slower answers — but this one I can answer fast, because the thing you're actually asking isn't about Dav, it's about Dell.

If Dav goes to Mako, he goes without me. Not because this circle has earned more from me than he has, but because Dell is my blood and she's standing closer to your side of that line than his, and a mother who follows a man away from her own child is a woman who's already stopped thinking clearly. I won't do that.

What I need from you in return is plain: if Dav moves toward Mako and I'm left standing here with one hand empty, I need to know this circle holds. Not as a courtesy. As a wall.
name: Ryn
